topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetic, Endogenous, and Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous mutational processes and inherited genetic predispositions with environmental exposures and epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma Pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of pathogen-driven malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical, Physical, and Promotional Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular and biochemical mechanisms by which chemical mutagens, metabolic activation, physical radiation, and tumor promoters drive cancer initiation and development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Mutagenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to evaluate carcinogens, ranging from mutational signature analysis and biobanks to animal models and in vitro assays.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core themes regarding environmental cancer risk and concludes with real-world risk-benefit considerations.
